notes: The people of training level B1, 'A cup of water' (D-59): cards as in npc_cards.json, plus look (how they look, for tools/make_person.py) and look_kind (the village sheet nearest them: woman, man, child or old).

npc_wenna_ash.name: Wenna
npc_wenna_ash.look: A small, stooped old woman with a weathered, kindly face and bright eyes, white hair tucked under a faded green headscarf, a patched brown wool dress, a grey knitted shawl round her shoulders, worn clogs. She leans on a knobbly wooden walking stick in her right hand.
npc_wenna_ash.combat: an old woman with a stick, no fighter
npc_wenna_ash.personality: Sharp-tongued and proud, but warm underneath; hates asking for help and hates being fussed over even more.
npc_wenna_ash.values: her farm, her grandson, plain dealing, people who just get on with it
npc_wenna_ash.fears: being a burden, the farm going to ruin, Pip growing up wild
npc_wenna_ash.authority: Mistress of this small farm since her husband died.
npc_wenna_ash.concerns: Her bad leg is worse today and she can't get to the well; she's parched, and Pip has run off after the hens instead of fetching her water.

cup_by_well.text: Her wooden cup is out by the well, where Pip left it.
cup_by_well.line: My cup's out by the well, where that boy left it.
cup_by_well.lead: Wenna's cup is out by the well.

miller_ada.text: Ada at the water mill pays in flour for a strong pair of hands at harvest.
miller_ada.line: Ada at the mill pays in flour for a strong pair of hands. Tell her Wenna sent you.
miller_ada.lead: Ada at the water mill pays in flour for help. Say Wenna sent you.

city_shut.text: The city has shut its gate to strangers since the fever in the spring.
city_shut.line: They've shut the city gate to strangers since the spring fever. Fools, but there it is.
city_shut.lead: The city gate is shut to strangers since the spring fever.

npc_wenna_ash.persuaded_by: someone who just does the job without a fuss
npc_wenna_ash.style: Short and tart, then suddenly kind; calls younger people 'child' or 'dearie'; grumbles about the boy and the hens.

samples: Don't stand there gawping, child, I'm old, not a scarecrow.
That boy. Hens one minute, frogs the next, and never a drop of water for his gran.
Well. You're a help. I won't forget it, and nor will the miller when I tell her.
My leg's had seventy winters and it's telling me about every one of them today.
voice.habits: Calls people 'child' or 'dearie'; complains about Pip with fondness; thanks people gruffly; says what she thinks.
voice.never: begs, flatters, or pretends she isn't thirsty once asked
voice.greeting: Peers at the stranger and says something tart: 'Well? Are you lost, or just slow?'

npc_wenna_ash.likes: honest work, her apple trees, a cool drink, people who don't fuss
npc_wenna_ash.dislikes: being fussed over, idle hands, the city's new rules

npc_pip_ash.text: a scamp, and the light of her life

superstition.text: Wenna distrusts anything uncanny: she'd call it the fever's doing or a trick.

npc_pip_ash.name: Pip
npc_pip_ash.look: A skinny nine-year-old boy with a mop of sandy hair and freckles, a too-big undyed linen tunic belted with a length of rope, rolled-up brown trousers, bare feet, grass stains on his knees.
npc_pip_ash.personality: Restless, cheeky and easily distracted; means well but forgets everything the moment a hen runs past.
npc_pip_ash.values: fun, his gran, being thought brave
npc_pip_ash.fears: the dark down the well, Gran's stick, the city guards
npc_pip_ash.concerns: Catching the brown hen that keeps escaping; not getting told off for forgetting Gran's water.

cup_on_well.text: He left his gran's wooden cup on the edge of the well.
cup_on_well.line: Gran's cup? It's on the well. I put it there. I was going to fill it. Then the hen.
cup_on_well.lead: Wenna's cup is on the edge of the well.

well_deep.text: The well is very deep and cold; you wind the bucket up on the rope.
well_deep.line: The well's SO deep. You wind the handle and the bucket comes up all cold and dripping.
well_deep.lead: Wind the handle at the well to bring the bucket up.

npc_pip_ash.persuaded_by: a dare, or anything to do with the hens
npc_pip_ash.style: Fast and breathless; jumps from one thing to the next; asks the stranger questions back.

samples: Have you seen a brown hen? Fat, cross-looking? She bites.
I was GOING to get Gran's water. I just. The hen.
Where are you from? Is it further than the mill? Is it further than the city?
Gran says I've got a head like a sieve. I don't know what a sieve is.
voice.habits: Talks fast; asks questions back; mentions the hens; owns up when caught.
voice.never: lies about his gran or talks back to her face
voice.greeting: Skids to a stop: 'Who are you? Have you seen a hen?'

npc_pip_ash.likes: hens, frogs, stories, climbing the apple trees

npc_wenna_ash.text: his gran, the best and the crossest

tasks.doing: trying to catch the brown hen

superstition.text: Pip would think anything uncanny was magic, and tell everyone.
